subject: Request: SLA carve-out for monthly batch windows + credit structure (StratusData)
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratusdata.com
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA request for scheduled batch windows and credit mechanics

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Redwood Dedicated offering looks promising for our inference workload. Before we move to contract, procurement has one ask around the SLA. We run a predictable batch processing window the first Sunday of each month (03:00–07:00 PT) that can require rolling maintenance on our side and occasionally a short scheduled downtime on provider infrastructure.

Because of that pattern, we need the contract to acknowledge a monthly maintenance carve-out and to adjust the uptime/credit mechanics for the Dedicated environment. Specifically, our procurement team is requesting: 

- A formal maintenance carve-out for the documented monthly batch window (first Sunday, 03:00–07:00 PT).
- A slight adjustment to the committed uptime floor for Dedicated from Redwood's standard 99.95% to 99.80% for the Dedicated instance backing our batch workloads.
- A monthly credit calculation that is simpler for our finance team to reconcile: credits expressed as a percentage of the monthly committed fee with a cap of 25% (rather than the existing uncapped formula referenced in the template).

I attached a short one-page note (Stratus_SLA_Request_2026-08-24.pdf) with the proposed language. This is not a refusal to accept Redwood's platform — it's an operational reality for us. Please let me know if the carve-out and the credit cap are acceptable or if you need more detail about our batch window and traffic profile.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director of Platform Ops
StratusData

[Attachment: Stratus_SLA_Request_2026-08-24.pdf (PDF)]

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request for scheduled batch windows and credit mechanics

Hi Elaine — really appreciate the clear note and for surfacing the batch pattern. Happy to work through wording that recognizes your operational window. A few quick points from our side: 

1) Maintenance carve-out: We can include a documented monthly maintenance window for the Dedicated deployment. We prefer to codify the carve-out as a scheduled maintenance window (first Sunday, 03:00–07:00 PT) plus a 1-hour buffer on either side for coordination, subject to advance notice.

2) Uptime floor: For Dedicated deployments we typically aim to hold to 99.95% availability in our standard template. Given your predictable window, we're willing to discuss 99.90% for the Dedicated tier as a compromise; moving down to 99.80% will materially change our operational guarantees and pricing. Can you confirm whether 99.90% would be acceptable?

3) Credit mechanics: We understand the desire for a straightforward monthly cap. Our commercial team can agree to a fixed cap expressed as a percentage of the committed monthly fee, but at 50% (rather than 25%) for Dedicated capacity given the fixed reserve costs we carry. We can also provide a more granular banded credit table (e.g., 99.90–99.75 -> 10%, 99.75–99.50 -> 30%, <99.50 -> 50%). I'll attach a draft amendment showing the proposed table.

Next steps: I'm attaching an initial draft amendment (redwood_sla_amendment_draft_1.pdf). If that looks reasonable, I will loop in our legal team to do a redline. Also copying Marissa (your account executive) so she can coordinate pricing implications and a short call with procurement if needed.

Thanks — speak soon.

— Aditya Rao
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood_sla_amendment_draft_1.pdf (PDF)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request for scheduled batch windows and credit mechanics

Hi Elaine,

Looping in legal to propose a concise redline. High-level comments:

- We can accept a documented monthly maintenance carve-out for a single scheduled four-hour window plus one-hour buffer each side; we will need to specify that the window is mutually agreed and can be rescheduled with 14 days' notice.
- For Dedicated capacity, counsel recommends a 99.90% uptime floor as Aditya suggested. Dropping to 99.80% is a substantive concession; if Stratus requires 99.80% we should adjust pricing/commitment levels accordingly.
- Regarding credits: we will propose a banded credit table tied to percentage availability (we find these clearer operationally). However, we can set an explicit monthly cap at 50% of the committed monthly payment for the Dedicated commitment.

I've attached a redline that: 1) inserts the carve-out language; 2) provides a three-band credit schedule; and 3) adds a requirement for a monthly operational review and a post-incident runbook delivery for any incident producing > 60 minutes of unplanned downtime.

If you can share the internal procurement approvers and confirm whether the 99.90% / 50% cap compromise is acceptable, we can produce a final DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SLA_Amendment_Redline_LB.docx (Word redline)]

From: Elaine Park <elaine@stratusdata.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@stratusdata.com>, procurement@stratusdata.com
Date: 2026-08-26T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA request for scheduled batch windows and credit mechanics

Laura / Aditya — thanks for the quick responses and for the detailed redline. I discussed your proposed compromise with procurement and finance this morning. High level:

- The maintenance carve-out as a scheduled, mutually agreed window with the 1-hour buffer is acceptable.
- StratusData can accept 99.90% uptime for the Dedicated instance, provided the monthly cap is 25% for the first 12 months only while we ramp (finance asked for that concession). After month 12 we'd accept 50% cap as standard.

If Redwood is comfortable with a 12-month transitional cap (25%) followed by 50% thereafter, we can route the DocuSign to our VP of Procurement, Martin Lopez (cc'd). Please send the final amendment and we'll aim to return a signed DocuSign within 5 business days.

Appreciate the flexibility — Elaine
Elaine Park
Director of Platform Ops, StratusData
elaine@stratusdata.com

Thanks — EL

[Requested next steps: Redwood to prepare final amendment reflecting: 1) scheduled monthly carve-out with buffer; 2) 99.90% uptime for Dedicated; 3) banded credit schedule with 12-month transitional cap at 25% then 50% thereafter. Please include DocuSign link when ready.]
